text:
alex: Quick sync — follow-up from the iterator/transport RFC. We need a concrete SDK surface decision (py/ts/go) before next sprint. Two high-level options:
- transport-first: expose flexible transport hooks to users (more power, more complexity)
- ergonomic-cursor: provide a simple high-level iterator that handles retries/resume for common cases (less flexible, better DX)
Thoughts?

tyler: Leaning toward ergonomic-cursor for 80% flows. Land the complex transport API behind an "advanced" flag or separate package.

maria: Agree. Most apps treat pagination/streaming as a single flow. If cursor does resume + sane backoff defaults, it covers 90% of customers.

sophie: Concern: we need clear semantics around idempotency + resume tokens. If a cursor hides retries, we must ensure it doesn't risk duplicate side effects when people call server-side ops in the middle.

alex: Good point. Proposal: cursor does retries only for safe read operations (generation/embeddings/paged listings). For any call flagged non-idempotent we expose an error and a low-level transport method.

jamie: Implementation nit: how does the resume token look cross-lang? Opaque string? Structured JSON?

alex: Prefer opaque base64 blob with a version tag inside. That keeps server freedom to change internals while SDKs just round-trip. Example: `v1:base64(<opaque bytes>)`. We add an SDK helper to decode for debugging but not rely on shape.

maria: For the ergonomics, propose the following minimal surfaces:
- Python: generator + context manager
- TS: AsyncIterable with `for await`
- Go: Iterator with `Next() (Item, error)` and `ResumeToken() string`

alex: Drafts: 
```
# Python
with client.list_messages_stream(...) as it:
    for chunk in it:
        handle(chunk)
    # it.resume_token() -> opaque string
```
```
// TypeScript
for await (const chunk of client.listMessagesStream(...)) {
  handle(chunk)
}
// client returns { resumeToken?: string }
```
```
// Go
it := client.ListMessagesStream(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() {
  item := it.Value()
  handle(item)
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { /* ... */ }
rt := it.ResumeToken()
```


tyler: Love it. What about retry/backoff policy defaults? Circuit-breaker vs hard fail?

sophie: Default: exponential backoff + jitter with a bounded total retry time (e.g., 30s for interactive endpoints). Provide pluggable policy object on the client for advanced users.

jamie: Also: when a cursor returns a resume token after partial iteration, we must document guarantees: resume token is server-provided, resume -> no-duplication is best-effort unless operation is idempotent. Make consumers aware.

alex: Agreed. We'll: 1) make resume tokens opaque and documented as "best-effort de-duplication"; 2) add explicit method `client.listMessagesStream({idempotency: 'guaranteed'|'best-effort'})` for customers who need stricter semantics (which will fall back to different server flows).

maria: Do we want to surface transport-level hooks for advanced users (e.g., custom http2 keepalive, alternate grpc transport)? If yes, how?

alex: Plan: keep the default client ergonomic. Provide an advanced `ClientBuilder`/`Config` where you can inject a Transport implementation (interface) in all languages. That keeps the main surface stable while allowing power users to swap transports.

jamie: Tests: we should add interop tests that: resume token round-trip, resume after transient error, resume after partial consume, and confirm no hidden side effects for flagged-non-idempotent endpoints. Add these to CI.

ci-bot: CI pipeline note: please add new interop tests to /tests/iterators and mark as flaky=false so they run in nightly integration.

alex: Next steps I propose:
- alex: update RFC with concrete APIs + code sketches (this week) PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2345
- tyler & sophie: prototype Python and TS cursor ergonomics (next sprint)
- jamie: spec resume token format + server contract doc
- maria: draft interop test matrix and CI plan

maria: acked. I'll own test matrix.

tyler: ack. I'll start TS prototype.

sophie: ack. I'll pair on default retry config.

alex: Thanks all. If there's no strong objections by EOD tomorrow we'll lock this for the sprint planning RFC follow-up. :thumbsup:
